data.name: Coastal Clean Front Yard
data.one_line: Salt-tolerant, breezy, and bright. A minimalist yet inviting design built to withstand Florida's coastal climate.
data.prompt_text:
Create a **front yard landscape** inspired by the *Coastal Clean Front Yard* style.
Prioritize **clean lines, salt- and wind-tolerant structure, and a bright, breezy appearance**. The layout should feel crisp, organized, and low-maintenance while capturing a Florida coastal aesthetic.

**Use the following plant palette as the core:**
– Pygmy Date Palm or Sabal Palm for vertical accents and tropical identity
– Saw Palmetto for hardy evergreen structure and texture
– Muhly Grass for soft motion and pink fall plumes
– Society Garlic or Agapanthus for edging and seasonal purple blooms
– White gravel or crushed shell for the ground plane to provide brightness and contrast

**Layer the design from front to back:**
• Edging plants (society garlic or agapanthus) along walkways and borders
• Mid-height grasses (muhly) in soft, flowing groupings for seasonal color
• Palmetto shrubs behind for evergreen structure and resilience
• Palms as focal points to define the entry or corners of the house

**Add optional hardscape elements such as:**
– A coral stone or paver walkway
– Decorative shell borders or edging
– Simple ceramic planters near the entry

**Adapt based on site conditions:**
• In high-wind areas, favor sabal palms for resilience
• In higher-salt exposure, emphasize saw palmetto and dune-friendly grasses
• For partially shaded inland sites, substitute coontie or dwarf holly for palmetto

Maintain the **bright, breezy, and resilient character** throughout — using plants that thrive with minimal care and remain polished year-round.

Only include plants suited for **USDA Zones 9–11 and Florida's hot, humid, coastal climate**.

Most importantly, please keep the house and structure the exact same. only the above changes to the front yard and landscape areas.
